Study X: Kaufman Assessment Battery for Children–Second Edition
Kaufman Test of Educational Achievement—Second Edition Brief Form

Measure IQ.evidence_source: Long term storage and retrieval (Glr) was measured with four subtests from the Kaufman Assessment Battery for Children–Second Edition (KABC-II; A. S. Kaufman & N. L. Kaufman, 2004): Atlantis, Rebus, Atlantis Delayed, and Rebus Delayed. Gc was measured using the Reading subtest from the Kaufman Test of Educational Achievement—Second Edition Brief Form (KTEA-II; A. S. Kaufman & N. L. Kaufman, 2005).

IQ modality.evidence_source: Atlantis. In this subtest, the participant is taught nonsense names for pictures of fish, plants, and shells. Rebus. The participant is taught words or concepts that are associated with rebuses (drawings), then "reads" aloud the phrases and sentences that are composed of these rebuses. Reading. This test is comprises two parts. The first part is word recognition, where the participants read words of increasing difficulty that do not follow phonetic rules. The second part is reading comprehension.

IQ Aspect.evidence_source: Long term storage and retrieval (Glr) was measured with four subtests from the Kaufman Assessment Battery for Children–Second Edition (KABC-II; A. S. Kaufman & N. L. Kaufman, 2004). Gc was measured using the Reading subtest from the Kaufman Test of Educational Achievement—Second Edition Brief Form (KTEA-II; A. S. Kaufman & N. L. Kaufman, 2005).

Creativity Measures.evidence_source: Creative Achievement Questionnaire (CAQ; Carson, Peterson, & Higgins, 2005).

Domain classified.evidence_source: Participants are presented with levels of creative achievement in 10 domains: visual arts, music, dance, architectural design, creative writing, humor, inventions, scientific discovery, theater/film, and culinary arts. Participant scores for each domain were recorded by adding all the endorsements for that category based on the weight of each question.

Number of studies.evidence_source: the authors decided to use the KABC-II for this study because it provides more measures of Glr by including Atlantis and Atlantis Delayed. In the current study, Cronbach's alpha coefficient for our sample of college students was r .91.

section_summary.extract_value: This section details the measures used in a single study. Intelligence was assessed using the Kaufman Assessment Battery for Children–Second Edition (KABC-II) for Long Term Storage and Retrieval (Glr) and the Kaufman Test of Educational Achievement—Second Edition Brief Form (KTEA-II) for Crystallized Intelligence (Gc). Creativity was measured through the Consensual Assessment Technique (CAT), the Creative Achievement Questionnaire (CAQ), and a Self-assessment of creativity (SAC). The text consistently refers to "this study" or "the current study" without numbering, indicating a single study.
